documents.title: Emergent Fractional Dimensionality and Spinor-Like Holonomy in Multi-Sheeted Pentagon Tilings

constraints: Graph is not vertex-transitive and cannot be flattened into a contiguous memory array.
affordances: Spatial hashing keyed by exact Q(sqrt5) coordinates and sheet index for O(1) neighbor lookups.

nodes.name: Emergent Fractional Dimensionality from Frustrated Pentagon Tilings
nodes.statement: The paper's research direction is to derive an emergent, non-integer effective dimension and spinor-like holonomy from a purely local 2D pentagon adjacency rule.

shape.descriptor: geometric frustration resolved by covering space, not curvature or aperiodicity

sources.heading: Abstract
sources.quote: We present a novel discrete geometric framework based on multi-sheeted, overlapping 2D pentagonal tilings.

nodes.name: Sheet Holonomy as Spinor Double Cover
nodes.statement: The sheet-index holonomy around a pentagonal vortex is analogous to the SU(2) to SO(3) double cover required by spinors.

shape.descriptor: two full loops needed to restore identity, like a spinor

similar_to.note: both concern fractional/discrete phase accumulation around a defect

sources.heading: 3.2. The Spinor Analogy
sources.quote: This requirement of multiple full rotations to achieve identity is the precise discrete geometric analogue of spinor holonomy.

nodes.name: Sheet Transitions as Anyonic Braid Statistics
nodes.statement: The sheet-transition group resembles a discrete braid group in which a glider looping a defect accumulates a fractional phase, mimicking anyonic statistics.

sources.heading: 3.3. Connection to Anyons and Braid Statistics
sources.quote: This mimics anyonic statistics observed in condensed matter and offers a fully discrete, coordinate-free toy model for topological quantum computing primitives.

nodes.name: Pentagon Frustration Mapped onto Discrete Gauge Bundle
nodes.statement: The systematic correspondence between pentagon edge-matching transitions and a discrete principal G-bundle connection maps geometric frustration onto gauge-theoretic holonomy.

sources.heading: Abstract
sources.quote: the resulting structure is a discrete principal $G$-bundle whose monodromy realizes spinor-like holonomy

nodes.name: Continuous Limit of the Multi-Sheeted Tiling Is Unknown
nodes.statement: It is unknown whether the multi-sheeted tiling converges to a smooth non-Euclidean manifold, a singular metric space, or a quantum-gravitational fractal as tile size shrinks.

sources.heading: 7.3. Open Questions
sources.quote: Does the multi-sheeted tiling converge to a smooth non-Euclidean manifold, a singular metric space, or a quantum-gravitational fractal in the limit of infinitely small tile size?

nodes.name: Regular Pentagons Cannot Tile the Plane Flatly Around a Vertex
nodes.statement: Three regular pentagons at a shared vertex sum to 324 degrees leaving a 36 degree gap, and four sum to 432 degrees producing a 72 degree overlap, so no flat monohedral pentagon tiling exists.

sources.heading: 2.1. The Frustration of Pentagonal Packing
sources.quote: Three pentagons share a vertex, summing to 324°, leaving an angular deficit of 36°

nodes.name: Multi-Sheeted Covering Space over the Plane
nodes.statement: A covering space M with projection pi to R^2 consists of an infinite stack of 2D sheets indexed by a discrete fiber group G, with pentagons identified by centroid, orientation and sheet index.

sources.heading: 2.2. The Multi-Sheeted Covering Space
sources.quote: We define a covering space $\mathcal{M}$ over the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$.

nodes.name: Identical Edge Adjacency Rule
nodes.statement: Two pentagons on possibly different sheets are adjacent iff their projected edges match identically in position and orientation, with the sheet transition governed by a transition function tau(e).

sources.heading: 2.2. The Multi-Sheeted Covering Space
sources.quote: Two pentagons $P_{i,s}$ and $P_{j,s'}$ share an edge $e$ if and only if... Their projected edges in $\mathbb{R}^2$ match identically

nodes.name: Exact Q(sqrt5) Coordinate Representation
nodes.statement: Pentagon centroids and orientations are represented exactly as elements of the real quadratic field Q(sqrt5), stored as 4-tuples of rationals, to make edge-equality tests exact.

sources.heading: 2.3. Algebraic Foundation
sources.quote: we mandate that all coordinates and orientations be represented exactly as elements of the real quadratic field $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{5})$

nodes.name: Float64 Arithmetic Causes Topological Tearing
nodes.statement: Naive float64 arithmetic accumulates rounding errors across edge-matching tests that spuriously merge distinct pentagons or miss true matches, tearing the covering space.
nodes.notes: Asserted as a design pitfall without a formal proof; treated as heuristic risk rather than proven theorem.

sources.heading: 2.3. Algebraic Foundation
sources.quote: producing _topological tearing_ of the covering space

nodes.name: Unconstrained Sheet-Stacking Densifies Projected Vertices
nodes.statement: Without a selection window, free orbits of the pentagonal rotation group densify in R^2, causing the projected vertex set to become dense and local finiteness to fail.

sources.heading: 2.4. Topological Regularization
sources.quote: free orbits of the pentagonal rotation group densify in $\mathbb{R}^2$; without restriction, the projected vertex set $\pi(\mathcal{V})$ becomes dense

nodes.name: Cut-and-Project Acceptance Window
nodes.statement: A pentagon is admitted into the simulation graph iff its lift into the 5D ambient lattice Z^5 projects within a bounded acceptance window W in the orthogonal complement of the chosen 2D physical subspace.

sources.heading: 2.4. Topological Regularization
sources.quote: A pentagon labelled by sheet $s$ is admitted into the simulation graph $\mathcal{G}$ if and only if its lift into $\mathbb{Z}^5$ projects within $W$.

nodes.name: Closed Loops Around a Vertex Accumulate Non-Trivial Sheet Holonomy
nodes.statement: A closed loop of adjacent pentagons around a vertex accumulates a net sheet-index shift given by the sum of transition steps along the path, and for loops enclosing a vortex this net shift is nonzero.

sources.heading: 3.1. The Vortex Mechanism
sources.quote: For a non-trivial loop enclosing a vortex defect, the net sheet transition $\Delta s_{\text{tot}} \neq 0$.

nodes.name: Connectivity (Hausdorff-Like) Dimension
nodes.statement: The connectivity dimension d_eff governs neighborhood volume growth V(r) proportional to r to the d_eff.

sources.heading: 4. Emergent Dimensionality and Fractional Geometry
sources.quote: The **connectivity (Hausdorff-like) dimension** $d_{\text{eff}}$, governing volume growth $V(r) \sim r^{d_{\text{eff}}}$.

nodes.name: Spectral Dimension
nodes.statement: The spectral dimension d_spec governs diffusion and return probabilities P_0(t) proportional to t to the minus d_spec over 2.

sources.heading: 4. Emergent Dimensionality and Fractional Geometry
sources.quote: The **spectral dimension** $d_{\text{spec}}$, governing diffusion and return probabilities $P_0(t) \sim t^{-d_{\text{spec}}/2}$.

nodes.name: Effective Dimension Lies Strictly Between 2 and 3
nodes.statement: Because pentagon overlaps and sheet transitions cannot be regularized into a periodic 3D lattice, the effective connectivity dimension is fractional and strictly between 2 and 3.

sources.heading: 4.2. The Fractional Dimension Regime
sources.quote: The effective dimension $d_{\text{eff}}$ is fractional: $2 < d_{\text{eff}} < 3.$

nodes.name: Spectral Dimension Is Strictly Less Than Effective Dimension
nodes.statement: Vortex-mediated bottlenecks make random walks sub-diffusive with walk dimension greater than 2, so via the Alexander-Orbach relation the spectral dimension is strictly less than the effective dimension and both exhibit dimensional flow.

sources.heading: 4.3. Dimensional Decoupling and Anomalous Diffusion
sources.quote: we expect a strict inequality $d_{\text{spec}} < d_{\text{eff}}$, with both quantities exhibiting **dimensional flow**

nodes.name: Alexander-Orbach-Type Relation Bounding Spectral Dimension
nodes.statement: The spectral dimension equals twice the effective dimension divided by the walk dimension.

sources.heading: 4.3. Dimensional Decoupling and Anomalous Diffusion
sources.quote: Via the Alexander–Orbach-type relation $d_{\text{spec}} = \frac{2 d_{\text{eff}}}{d_w}$

nodes.name: Isometric Cellular Automaton on the Sheet Graph
nodes.statement: An isometric cellular automaton assigns each pentagon a state updated by a local transition rule depending on the states of its graph neighbors, naturally suggesting 5-regular outer-totalistic rule families.

sources.heading: 5.1. Formal Definition
sources.quote: Each pentagon has exactly 5 edges, suggesting natural _5-regular outer-totalistic_ rule families

nodes.name: Causal Extension of the Isometric CA
nodes.statement: Reinterpreting the sheet stack as a foliation of space-like slices along a directed time axis, with admissible transitions restricted to respect causal ordering, converts the ICA into a causal cellular automaton analogous to CDT.

sources.heading: 5.2. Causal Extension
sources.quote: This converts the ICA into a **Causal Cellular Automaton**, analogous to the time-oriented building rules of CDT.

nodes.name: Gliders Split and Scatter at Sheet Transitions and Vortices
nodes.statement: Gliders traveling along a sheet can split at matching edges into components continuing on the same sheet and components jumping to another sheet, and vortex defects scatter gliders analogously to Aharonov-Bohm scattering.

shape.descriptor: topological defect as scattering center for discrete signal propagation

sources.heading: 5.3. Dynamical Properties
sources.quote: Vortex Scattering**: Topological defects act as scattering centers for gliders, rotating their direction of propagation or shifting their sheet index

nodes.name: Graph Is Not Vertex-Transitive, Barring Array Flattening
nodes.statement: Because the sheet graph is not vertex-transitive, it cannot be flattened into a contiguous memory array, requiring lazy generation and spatial hashing for simulation.

sources.heading: 5.4. Computational Considerations
sources.quote: Because $\mathcal{G}$ is _not vertex-transitive_, it cannot be flattened into a contiguous memory array as ordinary 2D CA can.

nodes.name: Global Consistency of Arbitrary Transition Choices Is Undecidable
nodes.statement: Determining whether an arbitrary choice of transition function tau yields a globally consistent infinite cover is undecidable in general, a variant of the Domino Problem, which the cut-and-project construction sidesteps.

sources.heading: 5.4. Computational Considerations
sources.quote: determining whether an arbitrary choice of $\tau$ yields a globally consistent infinite cover is undecidable in general (a variant of the Domino Problem)

nodes.name: Exact Adjacency Oracle
nodes.statement: The adjacency oracle computes a cell's edges exactly over Q(sqrt5), looks up matching edges by exact rational comparison, and filters candidates by the cut-and-project acceptance window.

sources.heading: 6.1. The Adjacency Oracle
sources.quote: All coordinates live in Q(sqrt(5))^2; comparisons are exact.

nodes.name: BFS Volume-Growth Measurement of Connectivity Dimension
nodes.statement: A breadth-first search from an origin cell out to radius R records the number of unique cells within each distance, and a log-log linear regression of N(r) against r yields the effective connectivity dimension via finite-size scaling across origins.

sources.heading: 6.2. Connectivity Dimension via Expansion Bounds
sources.quote: perform a linear regression on the log-log data: $\ln N(r) = d_{\text{eff}} \ln r + \ln C$.

nodes.name: Random-Walk Estimate of Spectral and Walk Dimension
nodes.statement: M independent random walks from an origin cell yield mean-squared displacement and return-probability statistics from which d_spec and d_w are fit, though the method is noisy at long times.

sources.heading: 6.3. Spectral Dimension via Random Walks
sources.quote: Random-walk estimates of $P_0(t)$ are, however, noisy at long times; we recommend treating them as a sanity check

nodes.name: KPM Spectral Analysis of the Graph Laplacian
nodes.statement: The graph Laplacian Delta = D - A is expanded in Chebyshev polynomials via the Kernel Polynomial Method to reconstruct the density of states, whose low-energy power-law scaling gives a high-precision spectral dimension, cross-checked with shift-invert Lanczos and finite-size scaling.

sources.heading: 6.4. Spectral Dimension via the Graph Laplacian and KPM
sources.quote: We expand $\rho(\lambda)$ in Chebyshev polynomials via the **Kernel Polynomial Method (KPM)**

nodes.name: Discrete Toy Model for Emergent Spacetime Dimensional Flow
nodes.statement: The predicted dimensional flow of d_spec(t) is proposed as a tractable discrete toy model analogous to IR dimensional reduction in CDT and asymptotic safety scenarios for quantum gravity.

sources.heading: 7.1. Connection to Quantum Gravity and Anyons
sources.quote: suggesting the framework as a tractable toy model for emergent spacetime

nodes.name: Algebraic Classification of Sheet-Transition Groups Is Open
nodes.statement: It is unknown what algebraic structure the group generated by sheet transitions has, whether it is finitely presented, and which choices of G and tau yield decidable, locally finite covers.

sources.heading: 7.3. Open Questions
sources.quote: What is the algebraic structure of the group generated by the sheet transitions?

nodes.name: Whether Standard CA Rules Remain Stable Under Fractional-Dimensional Lift
nodes.statement: It is open whether standard 2D CA rules such as Conway's Game of Life remain active and stable when lifted to this fractional-dimensional geometry, and whether 5-regular outer-totalistic rules can be tuned to Turing-universal behavior.

sources.heading: 7.3. Open Questions
sources.quote: Can 5-regular outer-totalistic rules be tuned to Turing-universal behavior?

clusters.name: From Angular Frustration to Spinor-Like Holonomy
clusters.summary: The exact angular mismatch of pentagon packing forces a covering-space construction whose adjacency rule produces nonzero sheet holonomy, later read as a discrete spinor double cover.

clusters.name: Numerical Pipeline for Fractional Dimension
clusters.summary: The exact adjacency oracle feeds BFS, random-walk and KPM procedures proposed to numerically certify the fractional connectivity and spectral dimension conjectures.

unresolved.description: The angular frustration facts (Section 2.1) are exact arithmetic consequences stated as derivations without a formal deductive apparatus; classified here as a lemma, but could be read as a mere numeric/geometric observation.

"Floating-point topological tearing" is asserted as an inevitable failure mode but no experiment or benchmark in the notes actually demonstrates it; kept as a heuristic pending empirical confirmation.
Section 7.2 (Fractional Statistical Mechanics) proposes Metropolis-Hastings Ising/XY simulations but gives no concrete claim, experiment, or citation precise enough to extract as a node.

References to CDT, Loop Quantum Gravity, and Group Field Theory in the Introduction are named research programs with no citation details (no author, year, or venue given), so only a generic research_program/reference context is recorded rather than dedicated reference nodes.
